notes: Complex dose-response paper with 3 experimental years (2016, 2017, 2018) and 2 biostimulant products (Kelpak SL and Terra Sorb Complex) applied at 2 dose levels and 2 spray frequencies to bean. The GT has 48 rows split into two groups: pairs 124-147 (replicates=3) and pairs 964-987 (replicates=4). Both groups cover the same 8 product×dose×frequency treatment combinations with 3 distinct ctrl_mean levels corresponding to the 3 experimental years. Only 24 JSON yield obs are available (8 combos × 3 years), sufficient for one-to-one matching with pairs 124-147 only. Pairs 964-987 (24 GT rows, replicates=4) are unmatched because all JSON yield obs are consumed. This second series likely represents a different cultivar or replicate block not separately captured by our extractor. Year-to-ctrl-level assignment: ctrl≈0.248/0.25 → year 2016 (JSON ctrl≈4971 g/m²), ctrl≈0.279 → year 2018 (JSON ctrl≈4968 g/m²), ctrl≈0.318 → year 2017 (JSON ctrl≈5182 g/m²). Note that Kelpak and Terra Sorb have different ctrl_mean sequences (0.2485/0.2786/0.3178 vs 0.25/0.2786/0.3178), suggesting separate experimental plots with slightly different baseline yields per product. Effect size agreement is weak to moderate: GT effects are all positive (consistently large, 3-42%), while JSON effects span positive and negative values across years, suggesting the GT averaged across years and possibly applied smoothing or aggregation. Unit discrepancy: GT means are in the range 0.25-0.37 (likely t/ha or kg/m²) while JSON means are ~4970-5800 g/m²; the ratio (~20,000) is inconsistent across product groups, possibly reflecting plot-size differences or unit confusion in the JSON extraction.
